Timber and intonation: You noticed that the bridge on acoustic guitars slants a bit? Everybody tells you that the 12th fret is exactly between the nut and the bridge, but if that were true, the bridge would be straight across. The reason is that strings aren't infinitely flexible, when you take them out of the pack, they're doing their best to straighten out. Likewise, as the string vibrates when installed on the guitar, it doesn't break exactly on the nut or fret and the bridge, it bends gradually to form the curve. Also, the upper harmonics resist bending in the exact mathematical point you would expect, so each upper harmonic is just a tad sharper than you'd expect. And since this mishmash of out-of-tune harmonics clashes with itself just a dab, the guitar has a unique sound all it's own.
